newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Electricidad mulls dividend after rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Electricidad mulls dividend after rate rise.

text.p: Venezuela's Electricidad de Caracas, the bellwether stock on the Caracas Stock Exchange is reviewing its dividend policy in the light of a recent tariff increase, a top company official said Tuesday.
"We're still very conservative and still checking our numbers, but it's clear we have to do something soon," Freddy Cabrera, executive director of sales, told Reuters.
Electricidad suspended nearly all of its regular quarterly cash and share dividends in 1996 due to delays in receiving approval for tariff increases.

The possible change follows a tariff increase authorized Friday of 5.16 percent for industrial and commercial users, and 30.2 percent for the residential users that account for over one third of Electricidad billing.

"Overall the rise translates into a 10.4 perent increase in our tariffs," said Cabrera. While that falls short of a hoped- for 13 percent rise "it does represent the first step in the slow elimination of cross-subsidies," he said.

Industry analysts have long cited Venezuela's system of cross-subsidies, under which higher industrial charges support lower residential billing, as a fundamental obstacle to government plans for electricity privatization.
"The government is studying the possibility of a new system for next year. I hope they stick to it," Cabrera added.

As Venezuela grapples with a steep domestic recession Cabrera foresaw flat sales for the second half of 1996, growing only "from the second quarter of 1997 onwards at between one and 1.5 percent -- mostly from industrial users outside Caracas."

Electricidad's recently approved first half of fiscal 1996 results show 8.9 billion bolivars in net profits on 62 billion bolivar of sales versus 19 billion bolivars in net profits on 102 billion bolivar of sales over the first half of 1995.
Figures are in inflation-adjusted constant June 30 1996 bolivars.
